svg.title: How Concordia was built: five steps, factory first
svg.desc: A vertical timeline of five steps. 1, mid 2030s: asteroids first, as metal-rich bodies are bagged and hauled to L5 for iron-nickel and carbon-rich ones follow for carbon, nitrogen and hydrogen; then lunar mining, refining and a mass driver bring the bulk. 2, the station starts as its own factory with a construction yard, power, radiators and an industrial plant, and workers live in small construction rings. 3, the 21 km superstructure and shielding go up around the yard. 4, rotor 1 is built stationary, tested, filled with air and spun up in small steps; first residents arrive in 2041. 5, rotors 2, 3 and 4 follow and the fourth rotor reaches full spin in 2044.

g.text: The station is its own factory
Asteroids first: metal-rich bodies bagged and hauled to L5,
then carbon-rich ones. Lunar mass drivers bring the bulk.
Yard, power, radiators, industrial plant. Workers live in
The 21 km truss goes up around the yard.
Shielding cassettes are added as it grows.
Built stationary, pressure-tested, filled with air, then
The rings become spaceport lounges and spares.
